AIMGF_FEATURE_GROUP_TOKEN_<REF>: The data-lake token of a feature group that was registered with `tokenRef: <ref>` (the reference upper-cased, `-` as `_`): the value AIMgF uses when it connects to the data lake. The database holds the name, never the value. Prefer `_FILE` (a mounted secret). A reference with neither set resolves to nothing; it never falls back to another secret.
AIMGF_FEATURE_GROUP_TOKEN_<REF>_FILE: File holding the data-lake token for `tokenRef: <ref>` (the `*_FILE` form of `AIMGF_FEATURE_GROUP_TOKEN_<REF>`; set only one of the two).
AIMGF_TIMEOUT_EMULATION_SECONDS: Seconds an emulation run may take before AIMgF fails it as `TIMEOUT` and notifies the caller. A request's own `timeoutSeconds` wins. Raise it for long emulations.
AIMGF_TIMEOUT_INFERENCE_SECONDS: Seconds an inference job may take before AIMgF fails it as `TIMEOUT`. A request's own `timeoutSeconds` wins. Real-time inference needs this short; raising it only delays the failure.
AIMGF_TIMEOUT_SWEEP_SECONDS: How often the AIMgF worker (`aimgf-worker`) fails the training, validation, emulation and inference runs past their deadline (default 60, at least 1), across all worker replicas (call flow 27e). Read once at the worker's start. A job read still sweeps too. Seconds, not a secret.
AIMGF_TIMEOUT_TRAINING_SECONDS: Seconds a training run may take before AIMgF fails it as `TIMEOUT` and notifies the caller (default 30 minutes). A request's own `timeoutSeconds` wins.
AIMGF_TIMEOUT_VALIDATION_SECONDS: Seconds a validation run may take before AIMgF fails it as `TIMEOUT` (default 15 minutes). A request's own `timeoutSeconds` wins.
AIMGF_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/aimgf/...` to. Change it only when AIMgF is not reachable as `http://aimgf:8000` (another service name, an external host).
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: Access key of the S3-compatible bucket for the `backup` profile's `db-backup` service (`docs/DISASTER_RECOVERY.md`). Empty: the AWS CLI looks for a role or profile instead. Used by no module.
AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: Region the AWS CLI signs `db-backup` requests for (default `us-east-1`; MinIO accepts any).
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: Secret key that goes with `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, for `db-backup` only. In an environment variable it is visible to anyone who can inspect the container; on AWS prefer an instance or pod role.
DME_PRODUCER_HEALTH_CACHE_SECONDS: DME: how long, in seconds, a producer's health answer is remembered when a type's status is computed (call flow 11c). Default 30; 0 asks the producer at every read.
DME_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/dme` to (Data Management and Exposure).
FOCOM_AUTO_REGISTER_RESOURCE_TYPES: `true`, `1` or `yes`: `POST /resources/provision` registers an unknown `resourceTypeId` in FOCOM's own resource types (named by its id) instead of refusing it with 404 `RESOURCE_TYPE_NOT_FOUND`. Off by default; nothing is called.
FOCOM_IMS_ENDPOINT: Path FOCOM advertises as the O2ims `infrastructureManagementServicesEndPoint` in an O-Cloud's registration. Change it when FOCOM is published under another path.
FOCOM_SMO_REGISTRATION_SERVICE: URL FOCOM advertises as the O2ims `smoRegistrationService` (where an O-Cloud registers with the SMO). Set it to the address the O-Cloud can reach R1 Termination at.
FOCOM_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/focom/...` to (O-Cloud inventory and O2ims).
GUI_ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED: `true`: a local `admin` account without an enrolled one-time code can reach only the enrolment routes (every other route answers 403 `MFA_ENROLMENT_REQUIRED`, and the GUI sends the admin to Account security). Needs `GUI_TOTP_KEY` (the start fails without it). Users of the identity provider are not affected: their provider asks for the second factor. Default `false`.
GUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD: Password of the GUI's `admin` user, set at first start. Empty: a random one is generated and written to `GUI_INITIAL_PASSWORD_FILE`, never logged. Changing it later does not change an existing user: use the user admin page.
GUI_AUDIT_EXPORT_DIR: A directory: `python -m app.retention` first writes the audit rows it is about to delete there as JSON lines, and deletes only the rows written. Empty (the default): delete without exporting. See docs/RETENTION.md.
GUI_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS: Days to keep a row of the GUI BFF's audit log (`gui_audit_log`) when `python -m app.retention` runs (from cron, or `kubectl exec deploy/gui-bff` on Kubernetes). 0 (the default) keeps them all. See docs/RETENTION.md.
GUI_COOKIE_SECURE: `true` (default): the session cookie is marked Secure, so a browser sends it only over HTTPS (http://localhost counts). Set `false` only for plain-HTTP access by a non-localhost name, such as a lab VM by IP.
GUI_DATABASE_URL: SQLAlchemy URL of the GUI backend's own database (users, audit trail, the generated JWT key). SQLite file by default; with several GUI backend replicas point them all at one shared database.
GUI_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds the GUI backend waits for each module's `/health`, `/ready` and `/version` before showing it as unreachable on the dashboard. Raise it on a slow network.

GUI_INITIAL_PASSWORD_FILE.description: File (mode 0600) the generated first `admin` password is written to when `GUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is unset. It holds a password but is a path, not a secret itself; read it once, then change the password.

GUI_JWT_ALGORITHM: Algorithm that signs the GUI session token: `HS256` (default) with the shared `GUI_JWT_SECRET`, exactly as before; `RS256` or `ES256` with the key pair in `GUI_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE`, public keys at `/.well-known/jwks.json`. A token whose header names another algorithm is refused. Changing it signs every user out. Any other value stops the start.

GUI_JWT_PREVIOUS_KEY_FILES.description: Comma-separated paths of PEM files (a public key is enough) holding the signing keys of earlier rotations. Under `RS256` / `ES256` a session signed with one of them still verifies, matched by its `kid`, and the public key is published at `/.well-known/jwks.json`; none of them ever signs. Remove a file to end the sessions of that key. Must match `GUI_JWT_ALGORITHM`; an unreadable file stops the start. Empty (default): none.

GUI_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE.description: Path of the PEM private key (unencrypted PKCS#8 or traditional; RSA of at least 2048 bits for `RS256`, EC P-256 for `ES256`) that signs the GUI session token. Needed with `GUI_JWT_ALGORITHM=RS256` or `ES256`, refused with `HS256`; mount it as a secret (the chart's `gui.jwtKeySecretRef`). No inline form. An unreadable or unusable file stops the start.

GUI_JWT_SECRET: Key that signs the GUI session tokens. Empty: the first backend instance generates one and stores it in `GUI_DATABASE_URL`, so replicas on one database agree. Changing it signs every user out.
GUI_LOCAL_LOGIN_ENABLED: `true` (default): the GUI backend accepts username/password sign-in (and the `/api/token` password grant for scripts). `false` turns both off so every operator signs in through OIDC; it needs `GUI_OIDC_ENABLED=true` (the start fails otherwise). Leave it `true` as the break-glass admin path unless the identity provider is the only way in by policy.
GUI_LOGIN_MODE: Who may use the password form: `both` (default) offers OIDC when it is configured and the local form; `oidc` refuses `POST /api/login` and the `/api/token` password grant for every account except a break-glass one, so the identity provider's MFA applies (needs `GUI_OIDC_ENABLED=true`, the start fails otherwise); `local` does not offer OIDC even when it is configured.
GUI_OIDC_ALLOW_HTTP: `true` accepts plain-http URLs for the issuer, the provider's endpoints and the redirect URI when the host is not localhost. Lab use only: the code exchange and the signing keys then travel unprotected. Default `false`.
GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID: The client id registered for the GUI at the OIDC provider; ID tokens must name it in `aud`.
GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET: The OIDC client's credential, when the client is confidential. Prefer `GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`; setting both is an error. Empty with no file: a public client, protected by PKCE alone.
GUI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE: File holding the OIDC client's credential (a mounted Kubernetes or Docker secret); one trailing newline is removed. An unreadable file stops the start.
GUI_OIDC_DEFAULT_ROLE: Role for a signed-in user none of whose groups is in `GUI_OIDC_GROUP_ROLE_MAP`: `viewer`, `operator` or `admin`. Empty (default): such a user is refused.
GUI_OIDC_ENABLED: `true` turns on OIDC sign-in (authorization code with PKCE) next to the local login: the sign-in page then offers 'Sign in with <GUI_OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME>'. Default `false`. With it on, the issuer, client id, redirect URI and a group-to-role mapping (or a default role) must be set or the backend does not start.
GUI_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM: Name of the ID-token claim that carries the user's groups or roles (default `groups`): a list, or a string split on spaces and commas. A dotted name reaches into an object, such as `realm_access.roles`.
GUI_OIDC_GROUP_ROLE_MAP: How provider groups become GUI roles: comma-separated `group=role` pairs, role one of `viewer`, `operator`, `admin`, for example `smo-admins=admin,smo-ops=operator,smo-viewers=viewer`. A user in several mapped groups gets the highest role. Evaluated at every sign-in.
GUI_OIDC_ISSUER: Issuer URL of the OIDC provider, e.g. `https://keycloak.example.com/realms/smo`. Discovery is read from `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, and ID tokens must carry exactly this `iss`. Must be https (http only for localhost or with `GUI_OIDC_ALLOW_HTTP`).
GUI_OIDC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI: Where the provider sends the browser after the end-session (RP-initiated logout) page, when it offers one; must be registered at the provider. Empty: the parameter is not sent and the provider shows its own page.
GUI_OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME: Name shown on the sign-in button, 'Sign in with <name>' (default `SSO`).
GUI_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI: Public URL of the GUI backend's `/api/oidc/callback` as the browser reaches it (for example `https://gui.example.com/api/oidc/callback`), registered as a valid redirect URI at the provider. Must be an absolute https URL (http only for localhost or with `GUI_OIDC_ALLOW_HTTP`).
GUI_OIDC_SCOPES: Space-separated scopes requested at sign-in (default `openid profile email`); must include `openid`. Add `groups` (or the provider's own scope) if the provider only puts group membership in the ID token on request.
GUI_OIDC_SCOPE_CLAIM: GUI-5: the ID-token claim that holds a user's region/tenant scope (`{"regions": [...], "tenants": [...]}`), given to the user at every sign-in as the role is; a claim that breaks the rules refuses the sign-in (`invalid_scope`), none is an unscoped user. Empty (default): scopes are set by an admin on the Users tab.
GUI_OIDC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds the GUI backend waits for each call to the OIDC provider (discovery, signing keys, the code exchange); default 10. A slower provider makes the sign-in fail with 'could not be reached'.
GUI_OPERATOR_PASSWORD: Password of the demo `operator` user created at first start. Empty: no such user is created. Does not change an existing user.
GUI_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS: Seconds a GUI session lasts after sign-in (default 8 hours); the user must sign in again after it. Shorten it for shared consoles.
GUI_TOTP_ISSUER: Name an authenticator app shows for the one-time code of a GUI account (the issuer in the otpauth:// link). Default `SMO Operator Console`.
GUI_TOTP_KEY: Key (at least 32 characters, for example `openssl rand -base64 32`) that encrypts the one-time-code secrets of local GUI accounts in `gui_user_totp` and keys the hash of their recovery codes. Prefer `GUI_TOTP_KEY_FILE`; setting both is an error. Empty with no file: enrolment is refused and an account that is already enrolled cannot sign in. Changing it makes every stored secret unreadable: reset the users' codes (Admin > Users) and enrol again.
GUI_TOTP_KEY_FILE: File holding the one-time-code key (a mounted Kubernetes or Docker secret); one trailing newline is removed. An unreadable file stops the start.
GUI_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS: How many reverse proxies stand between a browser and the GUI backend (default 1: the console's nginx). The sign-in lockout and per-source throttle take the client's address from the entry that many places from the right of `X-Forwarded-For`, which the nearest proxy wrote; what a client put further left is ignored. Set 2 behind an ingress in front of the console; set 0 when clients reach the backend directly (the header is then not believed). A wrong value (too low behind a proxy) makes every client one source, and a source throttle then affects everyone.
GUI_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds the GUI backend waits for an answer from R1 Termination when it proxies a page's request (default 30). A longer call is shown as a gateway timeout.
GUI_VIEWER_PASSWORD: Password of the demo `viewer` (read-only) user created at first start. Empty: no such user is created. Does not change an existing user.
IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS_SECONDS: Seconds an `Idempotency-Key` stays `IN_PROGRESS` before another request with the same key may take it over (default 300). Shorten it if a crashed request must be retried sooner.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL_SECONDS.description: Seconds a stored `Idempotency-Key` (and its replayable answer) is kept (default 24 hours). A retry after this runs again instead of being replayed.

INTENT_SERVICE_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/intent-service/...` to.
KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST: Set by Kubernetes in every pod. Credential delivery (`RAPP_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY=kubernetes`) calls the API server at this host; unset outside a cluster, which disables delivery. Do not set it by hand.
KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT: Set by Kubernetes in every pod: the API server's port (443 if unset). Used only by credential delivery. Do not set it by hand.
LOG_LEVEL: Log level of every module: DEBUG, INFO (default), WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. An unknown value is INFO with a warning. DEBUG also logs the probe requests.
MDAF_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/mdaf/...` to (analytics catalogue and reports).
MLLF_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/mllf/...` to: AIMgF, which serves the deploy gate since S2.2, until S2.4 deletes the prefix.
MLMR_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/mlmr/...` to: AIMgF, which serves the model registry since S2.1, until S2.4 deletes the prefix.
MOCK_O1_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS: Mock O1 adaptor: how often, in seconds, it sends a heartbeat to RAN NF OAM for each endpoint registered with its own URL (`MOCK_O1_SELF_URL`) that has had a first heartbeat, as a real gNB does, so the endpoint stays ACTIVE past RAN NF OAM's 90 s missed-heartbeat threshold. `0` or unset (the code default): off. `docker-compose.yml` sets 30.
MOCK_O1_OAM_URL: Origin of RAN NF OAM (for example `http://ran-nf-oam:8000`) that the mock O1 adaptor's emit routes (`/emit/alarm`, `/emit/pm-report`, `/emit/pm-file`, `/emit/heartbeat`, `/emit/software-phase`) send to. Unset: an emit route answers 409 unless the request names a `target`. Plain HTTP: not usable towards a RAN NF OAM that requires mutual TLS. Only for tests and demos with the mock.
MOCK_O1_PROFILE: Name of a vendor profile under `mock-o1-adaptor/app/profiles/` (SB-10; the shipped one is `example-du`). The mock then declares that vendor at `GET /capabilities` (name, services, transports), returns the profile's class defaults on `get-config`, and has no RESTCONF root if the profile does not speak it. `MOCK_O1_VENDOR_NAME`, `MOCK_O1_SUPPORTED_SERVICES` and `MOCK_O1_VENDOR_MODES` still win when set. Unset: the generic mock. An unknown name stops the mock at start. Only for tests and demos with the mock.
MOCK_O1_SELF_URL: Mock O1 adaptor: the URL it is registered under at RAN NF OAM (the start of an endpoint's `adaptorUri`, e.g. `http://mock-o1-adaptor:8000`); the periodic heartbeat (`MOCK_O1_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS`) is sent only for those endpoints. Unset: no periodic heartbeat.
MOCK_O1_SUPPORTED_SERVICES: Comma-separated O1 services the mock adaptor reports as supported in its capability answer, and the services it emits (FM: alarms, PM: reports, FILE: files, SWM: software phases, HEARTBEAT: heartbeats; an emit route for a service not listed answers 409). Only for tests and demos with the mock.
MOCK_O1_VENDOR_MODES: Comma-separated vendor modes (`O1_NETCONF`, `O1_RESTCONF`) the mock adaptor reports. Only for tests and demos with the mock.
MOCK_O1_VENDOR_NAME: Vendor name the mock O1 adaptor reports. Only for tests and demos with the mock.
MODULE: Name of the module a container runs. Set by the image (`MODULE` build argument), not by an operator. It names the module in logs, in `/version`, in its shared SME identity and (for the sample rApps) in the registry. Do not change it.
NETCONF_CRED_<REF>_CA_FILE: Path of the CA bundle that verifies the server of a NETCONF-over-TLS endpoint whose `credentialRef` is `<ref>` (upper-case, `-` as `_`). Required with its CERT and KEY.
NETCONF_CRED_<REF>_CERT_FILE: Path of the client certificate for the endpoint credential `<REF>` (NETCONF over TLS), or of the SSH credential's certificate where used. Mount it as a secret file.
NETCONF_CRED_<REF>_KEY_FILE: Path of the private key for the endpoint credential `<REF>`: the SSH key, or the TLS client key. A credential named by an endpoint never falls back to the shared `NETCONF_SSH_*` one.
NETCONF_CRED_<REF>_PASSWORD: Password for the endpoint credential `<REF>`, named by an endpoint's `credentialRef` (the database holds the name, never the value). Prefer `_PASSWORD_FILE`.
NETCONF_CRED_<REF>_PASSWORD_FILE: File holding the password for the endpoint credential `<REF>` (the `*_FILE` form of `NETCONF_CRED_<REF>_PASSWORD`; set only one of the two).
NETCONF_SSH_KEY_FILE: Path of the SSH private key RAN NF OAM uses for NETCONF endpoints without a `credentialRef`. Without it, and without a password, the session cannot authenticate.
NETCONF_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS: Path of an OpenSSH `known_hosts` file. When set, RAN NF OAM refuses an SSH server whose host key is not listed (never trust on first use); when empty, host keys are not pinned.
NETCONF_SSH_PASSWORD: Shared SSH password for NETCONF endpoints without a `credentialRef`. Prefer `NETCONF_SSH_PASSWORD_FILE`; set only one of the two.
NETCONF_SSH_PASSWORD_FILE: File holding the shared NETCONF SSH password (the `*_FILE` form of `NETCONF_SSH_PASSWORD`).
NETCONF_TLS_CA_FILE: Path of the CA bundle that verifies a NETCONF-over-TLS server, for endpoints without a `credentialRef`. All three `NETCONF_TLS_*_FILE` are required together.
NETCONF_TLS_CERT_FILE: Path of the client certificate presented to a NETCONF-over-TLS server, for endpoints without a `credentialRef`.
NETCONF_TLS_KEY_FILE: Path of the private key of `NETCONF_TLS_CERT_FILE`. Mount it as a secret file with mode 0400.
NFO_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/nfo/...` to (network function orchestration, O2dms).
ONBOARDING_REQUIRE_SIGNED_PACKAGES: `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on`: Onboarding refuses a package that is not signed by a publisher in `ONBOARDING_TRUST_STORE` (the package fails with `package signature: the package is not signed ...`). Needs `ONBOARDING_TRUST_STORE`: without it every package is refused, with a message that says so. Default `false`: an unsigned package onboards as before. A package that carries a signature is checked against the trust store whenever one is configured, whatever this flag says. See docs/RAPP_PACKAGING.md "Signing".

ONBOARDING_TRUST_STORE.description: Path of the accepted rApp publishers' public keys: one PEM ed25519 public key file, or a directory of `<publisher>.pub` / `<publisher>.pem` files (the file name is the publisher's name; dot-files are skipped, so a mounted ConfigMap works). Read for each package, so a changed key needs no restart. With it set, a package that carries a signature must verify against these keys (tampered, added or removed file, unknown publisher and wrong key are refused with the reason); an unusable store (missing, empty, not an ed25519 key) fails the package. Empty (the default): no signature is checked. Public keys are not secrets, so this is a path and not a `*_FILE` secret. The chart: `rappSigning.trustStoreConfigMap`. See docs/RAPP_PACKAGING.md "Signing".

ONBOARDING_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/onboarding/...` to (rApp package store).
PGBOUNCER_MAX_CLIENT_CONN: Compose `pooler` profile: how many client connections PgBouncer accepts in total (default 1000). Above it, new clients are refused.
PGBOUNCER_POOL_SIZE: Compose `pooler` profile: server connections PgBouncer keeps per database and user (default 20). Raise it with the modules' replica count; it must stay below Postgres's `max_connections`.
POSTGRES_SLOW_QUERY_MS: Compose: Postgres logs every statement slower than this many milliseconds with its text (default 500). `-1` turns it off, `0` logs all. Read it with `docker compose logs postgres`.
R1_AUDIT: `on` (default): R1 Termination writes a hash-chained audit row for every authenticated change that reaches it. `off`, `false`, `0` or `no` stops writing; do not switch it off in production.
R1_BOOTSTRAP_KEY: Shared key that `GET /bootstrap` requires in the `X-Bootstrap-Key` header. Unset (the default): `/bootstrap` is open. Set the same value as `SMO_BOOTSTRAP_KEY` on every service that calls the gateway. Give the value or the `_FILE` form, not both.
R1_BOOTSTRAP_KEY_FILE: Path of a file holding `R1_BOOTSTRAP_KEY` (a mounted Secret). Give this or `R1_BOOTSTRAP_KEY`, not both.
R1_DEMO_RAPP_PM_REPORTS: `on` (`true`, `1`, `yes`) lets an rApp send `POST /ran-nf-oam/pm-reports` through R1 Termination, the PM an NF reports, which the sample rApps' Demo / simulation buttons send when they play the network (`docs/GUI_DEMO_GUIDE.md`); each such call is logged. `off` (the default): refused to an rApp like any change outside the rApp allow-list (403 `ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED`). For a demo stack only: an rApp with it on can put any PM it likes into the platform.
R1_GATEWAY_URL: Address every module (and rApp) uses to reach R1 Termination for calls to other modules and for `/bootstrap`. Change it when the gateway is not `http://r1-termination:8000` from the module's network.
R1_INTROSPECTION_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES: Most answers R1 Termination keeps while `R1_INTROSPECTION_CACHE_SECONDS` is above 0 (default 10000); the oldest goes first when it is full. Read once at start. Per replica.
R1_INTROSPECTION_CACHE_SECONDS: Seconds R1 Termination reuses SME's answer about a bearer token instead of asking SME on every request (default `30` in `docker-compose.yml` and the chart since release 0.8.0; the code's own default and `0` mean off: every request asks SME). A token revoked at SME (its invoker offboarded) is honoured for at most this long after the revocation, by any replica; the replica a revocation goes through stops at once. A wrong token is remembered for at most 5 seconds; SME not answering is never cached (still 503). A change of an invoker's role is seen after at most this long too. An unreadable or negative value leaves it off.
R1_INTROSPECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds R1 Termination waits for SME's token introspection (default 5). If SME is slower the call is refused with 503, not let through.
R1_KILL_CACHE_SECONDS: Seconds R1 Termination caches whether an invoker is stopped (default 3). A kill switch thrown at RAN NF OAM bites at the gateway within this time. `0` checks the database on every change.
R1_KILL_SWITCH: `on` (default): R1 Termination refuses every change by a stopped rApp with 403 `RAPP_KILLED`. `off`, `false`, `0` or `no` turns the gateway's enforcement off (RAN NF OAM's own check stays).
R1_KILL_SWITCH_SCHEMA: Database schema of RAN NF OAM's `rapp_kill` table that the gateway reads. Compose and the chart set `ran_nf_oam`; unset resolves through the search path (SQLite tests, unmigrated databases).
R1_MAX_BODY_BYTES: Largest request body R1 Termination accepts, in bytes (default 1 MiB), else 413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`. Applies to every route except the overrides below.
R1_MAX_BODY_OVERRIDES: Per-path body limits as `<path-pattern>=<bytes>,...` (default: the model artifact upload `/mlmr/models/*/artifact` and the rApp package upload `/onboarding/packages/upload`, each at 50 MiB). Setting it replaces the defaults, so repeat those entries if you still need them.
R1_OPERATOR_API_CACHE_SECONDS: Seconds R1 Termination caches the operator API base a rApp instance registered at rApp Management (default 5), for the `/rapps/{instanceId}/operator/...` prefix. A registration, a change or a terminated instance bites within this time. `0` asks rApp Management on every call.
R1_PUBLIC_BASE_URL: Origin (no path) consumers outside the compose network use for R1 Termination, such as `https://localhost:8443`. `/bootstrap` advertises SME's token endpoint under it; empty names SME on the internal network. Set it behind a TLS edge.
R1_RATE_BURST: Size of each invoker's token bucket at R1 Termination: how many requests it may make in a burst (default 200). Per replica of the gateway.
R1_RATE_PER_SECOND: Requests per second R1 Termination refills each invoker's bucket with (default 100); above it the caller gets 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`. `0` turns the limit off. Per replica.
R1_RATE_STORE: Where the gateway's per-caller token buckets live: `memory` (default, one budget per replica) or `postgres` (one budget across replicas, in the `rate_bucket` table; falls back to a per-replica bucket for a few seconds when the database errors). Read once at start; any other value stops the service.
R1_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds R1 Termination waits for a backend module's answer to a proxied call (default 60); then the caller gets a gateway timeout. Long-running calls should be asynchronous jobs, not a larger value.
R1_URL: Address the GUI backend reaches R1 Termination at, for health probes, `/bootstrap` and every proxied page request (default `http://r1-termination:8000`).
RAN_ANALYTICS_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/ran-analytics/...` to.
RAN_NF_OAM_CM_SNAPSHOTS: `true` (default): RAN NF OAM reads and stores the configuration before and after each sub-change of a config job, for `config-history` and rollback previews. `false`, `0` or `no` skips the extra read and the table.
RAN_NF_OAM_CM_SNAPSHOT_RETENTION_DAYS: Days a configuration snapshot is kept before `POST /config-history/purge` may delete it. `0` (default) keeps them for ever. Nothing deletes on its own: an operator or scheduler calls the purge.
RAN_NF_OAM_DISPATCH_RETRY_BUDGET_SECONDS: Seconds in total RAN NF OAM keeps retrying a NETCONF dispatch for a caller that must be answered in time (default 35). When the next delay would pass it, the job fails instead.
RAN_NF_OAM_ENFORCE_MO_TREE: `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on`: a write to a managed object that is not in the managed-object containment tree is refused (`MANAGED_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`) before anything is sent. Off by default.
RAN_NF_OAM_KPI_GUARD_GRACE_MINUTES: Minutes after a config job's observation window ends that the worker still runs its KPI guard (default 60); later it is left unchecked. `0` runs it only in the window.
RAN_NF_OAM_KPI_MAX_FILES: Most performance files one KPI query reads (default 2000). When more match, the answer says `truncated`. Raise it only with the memory and time it costs.
RAN_NF_OAM_MSAC_REACH: `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on` (MGT-2): the TS 28.319 access rules that guard CM writes also guard config reads and history, PM and FM subscription create, alarm acknowledge and clear, software-management jobs and the file routes, and leave out of every list route (alarms, subscriptions, jobs, endpoints, managed elements, cell guards, KPIs, the topology and the managed-object tree) what the caller may not read and make a subscription delete answer 204 without removing it (MGT-2.6), for a caller that is a registered MSAC Identity (matched on the invoker id the gateway vouches for). Off by default, so an Identity made for writes does not start refusing reads on upgrade.
RAN_NF_OAM_NETCONF_RETRY_DELAYS: Comma-separated seconds RAN NF OAM waits before each NETCONF attempt (default `0,5,10,20`: four tries). The number of values is the number of attempts.
RAN_NF_OAM_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/ran-nf-oam/...` to (O1 management, alarms, CM and PM).
RAN_NF_OAM_VES_PASSWORD: Password of the VES event listener (`POST /ves/eventListener/v7`, SB-7), the HTTP Basic credential an O1 adaptor posts with. Unset (the default): the listener does not exist and answers 404. Give this or `RAN_NF_OAM_VES_PASSWORD_FILE`, not both.
RAN_NF_OAM_VES_PASSWORD_FILE: Path of a file holding `RAN_NF_OAM_VES_PASSWORD` (a mounted Secret). Give this or the variable, not both; both set, or a file that cannot be read, closes the listener (503).
RAN_NF_OAM_VES_USERNAME: User name of the VES event listener's HTTP Basic credential (default `ves`). Used only when the listener is switched on by giving it a password.
RAN_NF_OAM_WINDOW_EXPIRE_SECONDS: Seconds between runs of the RAN NF OAM worker's `expire-windows` task (default 30, at least 1), which ends a config job still waiting (`PENDING_APPROVAL` or `SCHEDULED`) when its change window has closed (MGT-4.5). A job is expired at most this long, plus a worker tick (`SMO_WORKER_TICK_SECONDS`), after `window_end`. Read at worker start.
RAN_NF_OAM_WINDOW_START_ATTEMPTS: How many consecutive starts of one approved (`SCHEDULED`) config job may fail unexpectedly (an error that is not a safeguard refusal) before the RAN NF OAM worker ends it `FAILED` with `haltedReason` `START_ERROR_LIMIT` (default 5, at least 1; MGT-4.4). The count is kept on the job, so it survives a worker restart and is shared by replicas, and a successful start clears it. Read at worker start.
RAN_NF_OAM_WINDOW_START_SECONDS: Seconds between runs of the RAN NF OAM worker's `start-due-windows` task (default 15, at least 1), which starts an approved (`SCHEDULED`) config job once its change window has opened (MGT-4.4). A job starts at most this long, plus a worker tick (`SMO_WORKER_TICK_SECONDS`), after the window opens. Read at worker start.
RAPP_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY: `none` (default): an rApp's client credentials are returned only in the instantiate answer. `kubernetes`: rApp Management also writes them to a Kubernetes Secret in `RAPP_K8S_NAMESPACE`. Anything else is `none`.
RAPP_K8S_CA_FILE: Path of the CA bundle that verifies the Kubernetes API server for credential delivery (the pod's service-account `ca.crt`). Delivery needs host, namespace, token and CA all set.
RAPP_K8S_NAMESPACE: Namespace the per-rApp credential Secrets are created in. Required for `RAPP_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY=kubernetes`; the pod's service account needs create and delete on Secrets there.
RAPP_K8S_TOKEN_FILE: Path of the service-account token file used to call the Kubernetes API for credential delivery (normally `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`).
RAPP_MGMT_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/rapp-mgmt/...` to (rApp lifecycle).
READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds each `/ready` check (database, SME token) may take before it is reported as `timeout` (default 3). Keep it below the orchestrator's probe timeout.
SAFEGUARD_EVENT_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS: Seconds between two safeguard-refusal notifications for the same rApp and reason at RAN NF OAM (default 60), so a looping rApp does not flood subscribers. `0` notifies every refusal.
SAFEGUARD_REFUSAL_RETENTION_DAYS: Days a recorded safeguard refusal is kept before the purge route may delete it. `0` (default) keeps them for ever. Compose passes it through from `.env`.
SA_SMOS_O1_CM_HANDLER_URL: URL where the Intent Service pushes new O1 CM intents to SA SMOS's handler (default `http://sa-smos:8000/o1-cm-handler/intents`). Change it if SA SMOS has another address.
SA_SMOS_REPORTS_URL: Base URL MDAF pushes an assurance monitor's reports to (`<base>/monitors/{id}/reports`, call flow 04b; default `http://sa-smos:8000`, https under mTLS). Change it if SA SMOS has another address.
SA_SMOS_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/sa-smos/...` to (service assurance).
SME_ALLOW_OPEN_ENROLLMENT: `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on`: SME accepts invoker registration with no enrollment secret (role `internal`). Only for a lab with `SMO_ENROLLMENT_SECRET` unset; never in production.

SME_TOKEN_AUDIENCE.description: Audience SME requires in a client assertion for its token endpoint. Empty: `<SME_URL>/oauth2/token`. Set it when SME is published under another public URL than the one it is called by.

SME_URL: Address of SME: where R1 Termination forwards `/sme/...`, the base of SME's own token-endpoint audience, and (GUI backend) an optional override of the token endpoint otherwise discovered from `/bootstrap`.
SMO_ALLOW_SQLITE_FALLBACK: `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on`: when `SMO_DATABASE_URL` is not set, use an in-memory SQLite database instead of refusing to start. For unit tests only (every test suite's `conftest.py` sets it); never set it on a deployed service, where a missing database URL must stop the process rather than keep data in memory. Merely importing pytest does not enable it.
SMO_BACKUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS: Seconds between off-site backups by the `db-backup` service (default 600). The recovery point objective is this plus the time one backup takes, so it must stay well under 900 (`docs/DISASTER_RECOVERY.md`).
SMO_BACKUP_KEEP_MIN: Retention floor of `scripts/dr_backup.sh`: this many of the newest backup sets are kept whatever their age (default 5).
SMO_BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS: Retention of `scripts/dr_backup.sh`: backup sets older than this many days are deleted from the bucket after each successful upload, but never below `SMO_BACKUP_KEEP_MIN` sets (default 14).
SMO_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET: Bucket that receives the off-site backups. Empty (the default) and the `db-backup` service refuses to run; `scripts/dr_backup.sh`, `dr_fetch.sh` and `dr_drill.sh` read it too.
SMO_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT: Endpoint URL of an S3-compatible store that is not AWS (MinIO: `http://minio:9000`). Empty: AWS S3.
SMO_BACKUP_S3_PREFIX: Key prefix inside the bucket (default `smo`); each backup is a directory `<prefix>/<UTC timestamp>/` and `<prefix>/latest.json` names the newest.
SMO_BACKUP_S3_SSE: Server-side encryption requested on each upload: `AES256` or `aws:kms`. Empty: the bucket's own default applies.
SMO_BOOTSTRAP_KEY: The key `R1Client` (and the GUI backend's own client) sends as `X-Bootstrap-Key` when it discovers the gateway's endpoints; must equal the gateway's `R1_BOOTSTRAP_KEY`. Unset: nothing is sent.
SMO_BOOTSTRAP_KEY_FILE: Path of a file holding `SMO_BOOTSTRAP_KEY` (a mounted Secret). Give this or `SMO_BOOTSTRAP_KEY`, not both.
SMO_BUILD_SHA: Git commit of the build, baked into the image (`SMO_BUILD_SHA` build argument; compose reads it from your environment). Answered by `GET /version` and shown in the GUI. `unknown` when not given.
SMO_BUILT_AT: UTC time of the build (ISO 8601), baked into the image like `SMO_BUILD_SHA` and answered by `GET /version`. `unknown` when not given.
SMO_BUSINESS_METRICS_TTL_SECONDS: How long, in seconds, the scrape-time state gauges (rApp packages and instances, intents, outbox rows) are cached before the database is queried again. Keeps a busy Prometheus from querying on every scrape.
SMO_DATABASE_PASSWORD: Password put into `SMO_DATABASE_URL` when the URL has none. Compose and the chart mount it as a file instead (`SMO_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE`, from `db_password*`). Set only one of the two.
SMO_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE: File holding the database password (a Compose secret or Kubernetes Secret volume); a trailing newline is removed. The `*_FILE` form of `SMO_DATABASE_PASSWORD`.
SMO_DATABASE_URL: SQLAlchemy URL of the shared PostgreSQL database every module uses (without the password when the file form is used). Empty: the module refuses to start (unit tests opt in to an in-memory SQLite with `SMO_ALLOW_SQLITE_FALLBACK`).
SMO_DATABASE_URL_FILE: File holding the whole database URL, for deployments that keep the URL itself in a secret store (the `*_FILE` form of `SMO_DATABASE_URL`).
SMO_DB_HOST: Compose: host of Postgres in every module's database URL (default `postgres`). Set it to `pgbouncer` for the `pooler` profile, or to an external database host.
SMO_DB_IDLE_IN_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS: Milliseconds a connection may sit idle inside a transaction before Postgres ends its session (default 300000, 5 minutes). `0` disables it. Ignored behind a pooler (its server connections set it).
SMO_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW: Extra connections each process may open beyond `SMO_DB_POOL_SIZE` under load (default 10). Total per process is pool size plus this; multiply by workers and replicas against Postgres's `max_connections`.
SMO_DB_POOLER: `transaction` or `session` when the modules connect through PgBouncer (anything else is refused). `transaction` also turns off prepared statements; the pooler then owns the session limits. Empty: direct to Postgres.
SMO_DB_POOL_RECYCLE_SECONDS: Seconds after which a pooled connection is replaced (default 1800), so a firewall or pooler idle timeout does not hand out a dead one. `0` or less never recycles.
SMO_DB_POOL_SIZE: Connections each process keeps open to Postgres (default 5). Raise it with concurrency; count it per worker and replica against `max_connections`.
SMO_DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds a request waits for a free pooled connection before failing (default 30). A frequent timeout means the pool is too small or queries are too slow.
SMO_DB_PORT: Compose: port of Postgres in every module's database URL (default 5432); `6432` for PgBouncer.
SMO_DB_PREPARE_THRESHOLD: psycopg server-side prepared-statement threshold: a number of executions, or `off`. Unset: psycopg's default, except behind a transaction pooler where it is off. Set `off` for any pooler that does not support prepared statements.

SMO_DB_ROLE_PASSWORD_DIR.description: Directory `db_roles.py` (the `migrate` service) reads each module's database password file `db_password_<module>` from (default `/run/secrets`). A path, not a secret.

SMO_DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS: Milliseconds Postgres lets one statement run before cancelling it (default 30000). `0` disables it. Ignored behind a pooler, whose server connections set it.
SMO_ENROLLMENT_SECRET: Secret an SMO module presents to SME when it registers as an invoker, and SME requires. Empty: SME refuses registration unless `SME_ALLOW_OPEN_ENROLLMENT` is on. Prefer `SMO_ENROLLMENT_SECRET_FILE`.
SMO_ENROLLMENT_SECRET_FILE: File holding the enrollment secret (compose secret `enrollment_secret`, the Helm chart's Secret). The `*_FILE` form of `SMO_ENROLLMENT_SECRET`; set only one of the two.
SMO_EVENT_BUS: Which publisher the SMO event bus uses (docs/EVENTS.md): `table` (default; the shared `smo_event` table and, on Postgres, a NOTIFY at commit), `memory` (an in-process list, for tests) or `off` (publish nothing).
SMO_EVENT_LISTEN_URL: A direct Postgres connection (psycopg URL) on which a reader of the event feed LISTENs. Empty (the default): the module's own database URL, except with `SMO_DB_POOLER=transaction`, where the reader polls every 0.5 s instead (a transaction-pooling PgBouncer cannot deliver notifications). Set it to a direct connection there to be woken at commit.
SMO_EVENT_PURGE: `true` (default): the worker runs the event feed purge (`event-purge`). `false`, `0`, `no` or `off` turns it off.
SMO_EVENT_PURGE_SECONDS: Seconds between event feed purges by the worker (default 300).
SMO_EVENT_RETENTION_HOURS: Hours an event is kept in the SMO event feed before the worker's `event-purge` deletes it (default 24).
SMO_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds a module waits for another module's answer through R1 (default 30), and for callback deliveries. A slower dependency fails the call; raise it only for known slow routes.
SMO_IDENTITY_KIND: `module` (default): the process is an SMO service and registers at SME with the enrollment secret. `rapp`: it is an rApp and registers as an rApp invoker. Set by the sample rApps' deployment.
SMO_INVOKER_ID: Fixed SME invoker id of this module, when it is provisioned from a secret store instead of the shared identity table. Set together with `SMO_INVOKER_SECRET`.
SMO_INVOKER_SECRET: Secret of the fixed invoker identity named by `SMO_INVOKER_ID`. Overrides the identity kept in the database.
SMO_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: The Kafka brokers the relay connects to, `host:port[,host:port...]`; required when `SMO_KAFKA_RELAY` is on (compose: `kafka:9092`).
SMO_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID: The Kafka client id of the relay's producer (default `smo-<MODULE>`).
SMO_KAFKA_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT_MS: How long the relay's producer tries to deliver a message before it counts as failed and is sent again on the next pass (default 30000).
SMO_KAFKA_EVENTS_TOPIC: The topic the relay writes (default `smo.events.v1`). Must follow `smo.<owner>[.<stream>].v<N>`; a topic under `smo.teiv.` (smo-teiv's ingestion, TE&IV's alone) is refused. Compose's `kafka-init` creates it.
SMO_KAFKA_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: The largest event the relay sends (default 1048576); a larger one is skipped, logged and counted (`smo_kafka_produce_total{outcome="oversize"}`), never retried.
SMO_KAFKA_PARTITIONS: Compose only: the partitions `kafka-init` gives the events topic (default 6). Changing it later moves keys between partitions once.
SMO_KAFKA_RELAY: `true` makes this worker relay every event of the `smo_event` feed to Kafka after commit (ADR 0006, `smo_shared/kafka_relay.py`; one runner database-wide). Needs `SMO_EVENT_BUS=table` and an image built with `WITH_KAFKA=1`; without them the worker refuses to start. Default off. While on, `event-purge` keeps unsent events up to `SMO_KAFKA_RELAY_MAX_HOLD_HOURS`.
SMO_KAFKA_RELAY_BATCH: Events the relay reads and produces per batch (default 500, at most 500).
SMO_KAFKA_RELAY_INTERVAL_SECONDS: How often the worker offers the relay a run (default 1, so as often as the worker's tick allows); one run drains batches for up to 15 s.
SMO_KAFKA_RELAY_MAX_HOLD_HOURS: While the relay is on, how long past its time `event-purge` keeps an event the relay has not sent yet (default 72; ADR 0006 Q2). After that it is purged even though unsent.
SMO_KAFKA_RELAY_SETTLE_SECONDS: How old an event must be before the relay sends it (default 3): long enough for a transaction that took a lower sequence number to commit, so it is not skipped (docs/EVENTS.md).
SMO_KAFKA_REPLICATION: Compose only: the replication factor `kafka-init` gives the events topic (default 1: one broker).
SMO_KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM: The SASL mechanism with a `SASL_*` protocol: `SCRAM-SHA-512` (default), `SCRAM-SHA-256`, or `PLAIN` (refused unless the protocol is `SASL_SSL`).
SMO_KAFKA_SASL_PASSWORD: The relay's SASL password; prefer `SMO_KAFKA_SASL_PASSWORD_FILE`. Never logged. Both set: refused.
SMO_KAFKA_SASL_PASSWORD_FILE: A file holding the relay's SASL password (a mounted secret); see `SMO_KAFKA_SASL_PASSWORD`.
SMO_KAFKA_SASL_USERNAME: The relay's SASL user name (the principal the broker's ACLs name); required with a `SASL_*` protocol.
SMO_KAFKA_SECURITY_PROTOCOL: How the relay talks to Kafka: `SSL` (default), `SASL_SSL` (the production choice, with SCRAM-SHA-512), `SASL_PLAINTEXT`, or `PLAINTEXT` (logs a warning at start; the compose lab broker on the compose network only). TLS always verifies the broker's certificate and host name.
SMO_KAFKA_TLS_CA_FILE: A PEM CA bundle the relay verifies the broker's certificate with (unset: the system's).
SMO_KAFKA_TLS_CERT_FILE: The relay's client certificate (PEM) for a broker that wants mutual TLS.
SMO_KAFKA_TLS_KEY_PASSWORD: The passphrase of `SMO_KAFKA_TLS_KEY_FILE`, if it has one; prefer `SMO_KAFKA_TLS_KEY_PASSWORD_FILE`. Never logged.
SMO_KAFKA_TLS_KEY_PASSWORD_FILE: A file holding the passphrase of the relay's TLS key; see `SMO_KAFKA_TLS_KEY_PASSWORD`.
SMO_MIGRATE_LOCK_ATTEMPTS: Postgres only: how many times `scripts/migrate.py` tries an upgrade or downgrade that hit `SMO_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 10), pausing 1 s, doubling to at most 10 s, between tries; then the error ends the Job.
SMO_MIGRATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS: Postgres only: milliseconds `scripts/migrate.py` waits for any lock a revision takes (default 5000; `0`: no limit). On a timeout the whole upgrade rolls back, releasing every lock it held, and is tried again (MIGRATE-LOCK-HOLD).
SMO_MODULE_IDENTITY_STORE: `db` (default): replicas of a module share one SME invoker stored in the database (needs `MODULE`). `off`: each process registers its own, which adds a registration per replica and restart.
SMO_MTLS: `on` turns on mutual TLS between services (PR-SEC-2): the service serves HTTPS on its port and refuses a client without a certificate from the CA, and every call it makes presents its own certificate and verifies the server against the CA; `http://` peer addresses become `https://`. Off by default (plain HTTP, as before). Read once at start; needs the three `SMO_MTLS_*_FILE` files, and a missing one stops the process rather than serving plain HTTP. Values `on`, `1`, `true`, `yes`, `require`.
SMO_MTLS_CA_FILE: PEM file with the CA certificate(s) that sign every service's certificate, used to verify a client (server side) and the server (client side). During a CA rotation it holds the old and the new CA. Default `/run/mtls/ca.crt`. Only read with `SMO_MTLS=on`.
SMO_MTLS_CERT_FILE: PEM file with this service's certificate: its server certificate and its client certificate (extended key usages serverAuth and clientAuth, subject alternative name the service's name). Default `/run/mtls/tls.crt`. Only read with `SMO_MTLS=on`; a client rereads it when the file changes, a server loads it at start.

SMO_MTLS_INTERNAL_HOSTS.description: Comma-separated host patterns (fnmatch, for example `*.corp.example`) that count as inside the deployment, besides single-label names and `*.svc` / `*.svc.cluster.local`. A callback to an `https://` destination on such a host presents this service's certificate and is verified against the CA; any other destination is called as before, with the system roots and no certificate. Only read with `SMO_MTLS=on`. Unset: only the built-in rule.

SMO_MTLS_KEY_FILE.description: PEM file with the private key of `SMO_MTLS_CERT_FILE` (a path, not the key itself). Default `/run/mtls/tls.key`. Only read with `SMO_MTLS=on`.

SMO_MTLS_SERVE: With `SMO_MTLS=on`: `off` leaves this process serving plain HTTP while its own outgoing calls still use the certificate (the GUI backend, whose caller is the GUI's nginx). Default `on`.
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_ACCESS_KEY: The object store's access key id; prefer `SMO_OBJECTSTORE_ACCESS_KEY_FILE`.
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_ACCESS_KEY_FILE: A file holding the object store's access key id (compose: `secrets/objectstore_access_key`).
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET_COLD_PARQUET: The bucket of the cold telemetry tier, daily Parquet (default `smo-cold-parquet`; S3.11).
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET_MODELS: The bucket of model artifacts (default `smo-models`; S2.5 moves them there).
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_CA_FILE: A CA bundle for an `https` object store endpoint (unset: the system's).
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_REGION: The region the object store requests are signed for (Signature Version 4; default `us-east-1`, which SeaweedFS and MinIO accept).
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_SECRET_KEY: The object store's secret access key; prefer `SMO_OBJECTSTORE_SECRET_KEY_FILE`. It signs requests and is never sent or logged.
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_SECRET_KEY_FILE: A file holding the object store's secret key (compose: `secrets/objectstore_secret_key`).
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Seconds one object store request may take (default 60).
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_URL: The S3 endpoint of the object store (D10, `smo_shared.objectstore`), e.g. `http://objectstore:8333` (SeaweedFS, profile `objectstore`) or `http://minio:9000`. Path-style addressing.
SMO_OBJECTSTORE_WAIT_SECONDS: How long `python -m smo_shared.objectstore ensure-buckets` / `roundtrip` wait for a store that is still starting (default 60).
SMO_OTEL_ENDPOINT: OTLP/HTTP base URL of a collector or Tempo (for example http://tempo:4318). Empty (the default) turns span export off; the W3C traceparent is still passed on. Spans also need an image built with the OpenTelemetry packages (SMO_WITH_TRACING=1).
SMO_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO: Fraction of new traces that are sampled, 0 to 1 (parent-based: a request already in a trace follows its parent). Empty: every trace.
SMO_OUTBOX_INLINE_DRAIN: `true` (default): a module delivers its queued notifications right after the request that created them. `false`, `0`, `no` or `off`: only the sweep delivers them, which adds up to `SMO_OUTBOX_SWEEP_SECONDS` of delay.
SMO_OUTBOX_SEND_CONCURRENCY: Notifications one drain sends in parallel (default 8). Raise it for many subscribers; each is one outbound call.
SMO_OUTBOX_SENT_RETENTION_SECONDS: Seconds a delivered notification row is kept before the sweep deletes it (default 86400, one day). Failed (DEAD) rows are never deleted by this.
SMO_OUTBOX_SWEEP: `true` (default): the worker runs the outbox delivery sweep. `false`, `0`, `no` or `off` turns it off (then only inline drains deliver).
SMO_OUTBOX_SWEEP_SECONDS: Seconds between outbox delivery sweeps by the worker (default 5). It bounds the delay of a retried notification.
SMO_RETENTION_ALARMS_DAYS: Days to keep a cleared alarm before the RAN NF OAM worker deletes it (`purge-cleared-alarms`, hourly). An alarm still raised is never deleted. 0 (the default) keeps them all. See docs/RETENTION.md.
SMO_RETENTION_APPROVALS_DAYS: Days to keep an rApp action approval request after it was decided or lapsed before the RAN NF OAM worker deletes it (`purge-approvals`, hourly). A request still waiting is never deleted. 0 (the default) keeps them all. The decision record and the audit chain are not affected. See docs/RETENTION.md.
SMO_RETENTION_DECISION_RECORDS_DAYS: Days to keep a decision record (why an rApp acted) before the RAN NF OAM worker deletes it (`purge-decision-records`, hourly). Only a record already written to the audit chain is deleted, and the chain's rows (`audit_log`) are never deleted, so the chain still verifies. 0 (the default) keeps them all. See docs/RETENTION.md.
SMO_RETENTION_DME_RECORDS_DAYS: Days to keep a DME data record (by `produced_at`) before `dme-worker` purges it (task `purge-records`, hourly; call flow 12d). Default 0 keeps every record; `docs/RETENTION.md` proposes 30.
SMO_RETENTION_MDAF_REPORTS_DAYS: Days to keep an MDAF report before the MDAF worker deletes it (`purge-reports`, hourly). 0 (the default) keeps them all. See docs/RETENTION.md.
SMO_RETENTION_PM_FILES_DAYS: Days to keep a PM file (its content is the row; there is no file on disk) before the RAN NF OAM worker deletes it (`purge-pm-files`, hourly). 0 (the default) keeps them all. KPIs read PM files, so keep at least the longest KPI look-back. See docs/RETENTION.md.
SMO_RETENTION_WARN_ROWS: Rows above which a table whose retention is `0` (off) is reported: the worker's purge task (and `python -m app.retention` for the GUI audit log) logs one WARNING per table per day, and the worker exports the estimate as `smo_retention_off_rows{table}`. Postgres: the planner's estimate (`pg_class.reltuples`), SQLite: `count(*)`. Default 1000000; `0` never warns (the gauge stays). See docs/RETENTION.md.
SMO_ROLE_ENFORCEMENT: `enforce` (default): a role check that fails refuses the call with 403. `audit`: it only logs. Anything else is `enforce`, so a typo cannot switch protection off. Use `audit` only to trial a new role table.
SMO_SDK_RETRY: Python SDK (`smo_sdk`) in an rApp: `off` sends every SDK call once (no repeat after a transport error or a 429/502/503/504); `on` (the default) repeats them per the policy in `sdk/README.md`. Any other value stops the rApp at start. SMO modules do not read it. The Go and Java SDKs have no such variable (their policy is set in code).
SMO_SDK_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS: Python SDK: milliseconds of the first wait before a repeat (default 200); each following wait doubles, up to `SMO_SDK_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS`, with jitter between half and all of it. A whole number of at least 1.
SMO_SDK_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS: Python SDK: how many times in all a call is sent when it keeps failing for a transient reason (default 4, the first send included; 1 means never repeat). A whole number of at least 1.
SMO_SDK_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS: Python SDK: the longest wait between two sends, in milliseconds (default 5000), before jitter. A server's `Retry-After` may make one wait longer, up to 30 s. At least `SMO_SDK_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS`.
SMO_TIMESCALEDB: Whether `scripts/migrate.py` creates the TimescaleDB extension (D8) before the revisions run: `auto` (default) creates it when the Postgres has it and goes on without it otherwise; `require` stops the migration without it (compose's `migrate` and the chart's bundled Postgres set this); `off` never touches it. The chart takes it from `postgres.external.timescaledb` for an external Postgres.
SMO_VERSION: Release version of the build (for example `0.5.0`), baked into the image (`SMO_VERSION` build argument). Answered by `GET /version` and shown in the GUI. `unknown` when not given.
SMO_WITH_KAFKA: Compose only: `1` builds the DME worker's image with the Kafka client (the Dockerfile's `WITH_KAFKA` build argument, `requirements/kafka.txt`), which the event-bus relay needs (default `0`: images without it).
SMO_WITH_TRACING: Compose build argument: 1 installs the OpenTelemetry packages (requirements/tracing.txt) into the image. 0 (the default) builds the image without them.
SMO_WORKER_FAILURE_BACKOFF_SECONDS: Seconds a worker waits before running a task again after it failed (default 30), so a broken task does not spin.
SMO_WORKER_HEARTBEAT_FILE: File a worker touches on every tick (default `/tmp/worker-heartbeat`); the container health check reports unhealthy when it is a minute old. Change it only with the health check.
SMO_WORKER_METRICS_PORT: Port on which a module's worker process serves its own /metrics (task runs and last success per task). Unset by default: the worker serves no metrics port.
SMO_WORKER_TICK_SECONDS: Seconds between a worker's checks for due tasks (default 5). A task's own interval cannot be shorter than this.
SO_SMOS_URL: Base URL R1 Termination forwards `/so-smos/...` to (service orchestration).
RAPP_MGMT_REQUIRE_SME_REGISTRATION: `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on`: rApp Management refuses an instance's bootstrap (it stays DEPLOYING; 503 when SME does not answer, 502 when it refuses) unless every SME declaration of its package (`Files/Sme/providers`, `serviceapis`) is registered. Default `false`: the registration is best-effort and a failure is ignored. `deploy/helm/smo/values-production.yaml` turns it on. Call flow 01d.

RAPP_MGMT_SECRET_ROTATION_DAYS.description: Read by the rApp Management worker (`rapp-mgmt-worker`, `SEC-15.19`): rotate the secret of a RUNNING rApp instance (with a registered operator API) once it is older than this many days, the same renewal as Re-send credentials. Default `0` (also unset, negative or not a number): no automatic rotation, nothing is read or written. An instance whose workload cannot be reached is not rotated and is tried again at the next run; with `RAPP_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY=kubernetes` nothing is rotated. A number of days, not a secret. `docs/SECRETS.md`.

RAPP_MGMT_SECRET_ROTATION_MAX_PER_RUN.description: The most instances one run of the automatic secret rotation rotates, oldest secret first (default `10`, at least `1`), so instances that fall due together are rotated over several runs. Only used while `RAPP_MGMT_SECRET_ROTATION_DAYS` is above 0. A count, not a secret.

RAPP_MGMT_SECRET_ROTATION_SWEEP_SECONDS.description: How often the rApp Management worker looks for instances whose secret is due (default `900`, at least `1`), across all worker replicas. Read once at the worker's start. Only used while `RAPP_MGMT_SECRET_ROTATION_DAYS` is above 0. Seconds, not a secret.

GUI_ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES: Per-account sign-in cool-down (`SEC-15.11b`): how many failed sign-ins of one user name, from any addresses together, inside `GUI_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_SECONDS` start a cool-down for that name (default 20). `0` switches the cool-down off. The older per-address counters are not affected. Unknown names count like real ones.
GUI_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_SECONDS: Seconds in which `GUI_ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES` failures of one user name must fall to start a cool-down (default 600); also how long a quiet name's counter takes to forget, with no sign-in able to reset it. Must be 1 or more while the cool-down is on.
GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS: Seconds a user name is refused (429, a right password included) after it trips the per-account counter (default 60). Each repeat, after another `GUI_ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES` failures, is twice as long up to `GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_MAX_SECONDS`. Kept short on purpose: anyone can make a name fail, so a long value would let an attacker keep a real person out. Must be 1 or more while the cool-down is on.
GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_MAX_SECONDS: The longest a per-account cool-down grows to (default 300). Must not be less than `GUI_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`, or the backend does not start.
SMO_IDENTITY_KEY: Key (at least 32 characters, for example `openssl rand -base64 32`) that encrypts the secrets of the SME identities kept in the shared `module_identity` table (the modules' own and the rApp instances') at rest, AES-256-GCM, stored as `enc:v1:`. Prefer `SMO_IDENTITY_KEY_FILE`; setting both is an error, and so is a shorter key (the process does not start). Every replica of every module needs the same key. Empty with no file: secrets are stored in clear as before, and a row that is already encrypted cannot be read (the module gets no token and logs an error naming this variable). After setting it run `python -m smo_shared.module_identity encrypt-existing` once. Losing it means re-sending each instance's credentials and clearing the modules' rows (docs/SECRETS.md).
SMO_IDENTITY_KEY_FILE: File holding the identity key (a mounted Kubernetes or Docker secret); one trailing newline is removed. An unreadable file stops the start.
SMO_IDENTITY_PREVIOUS_KEY: The identity key of the rotation before this one, read-only: rows sealed with it are still read (and counted in `smo_identity_unencrypted_reads_total{kind="previous-key"}`) while new writes use `SMO_IDENTITY_KEY`. Needs `SMO_IDENTITY_KEY` and must differ from it. Run `python -m smo_shared.module_identity encrypt-existing` to move the old rows to the new key, then remove this. Prefer `SMO_IDENTITY_PREVIOUS_KEY_FILE`.
SMO_IDENTITY_PREVIOUS_KEY_FILE: File holding the previous identity key; same rules as `SMO_IDENTITY_KEY_FILE`.
ENERGY_SAVING_SCHEDULE_TICK_SECONDS: How often the EnergySaving rApp's worker (`energy-saving-rapp-worker`) looks for instances due a scheduled pass (default 15, at least 1), across all worker replicas (call flow 22e). An instance is due when its `evaluateEverySeconds` (instance configuration, 60 to 86400; absent: manual only) has passed since its last pass. Read once at the worker's start. Seconds, not a secret.
MOBILITY_SCHEDULE_TICK_SECONDS: How often the Mobility Optimization rApp's worker (`mobility-optimization-rapp-worker`) looks for instances due a scheduled pass (default 15, at least 1), across all worker replicas (call flow 23f). An instance is due when its `evaluateEverySeconds` (instance configuration, 60 to 86400; absent: manual only) has passed since its last pass; the KPI check of a CIO change needs a pass about an hour after it. Read once at the worker's start. Seconds, not a secret.
COVERAGE_SCHEDULE_TICK_SECONDS: How often the Coverage Optimization rApp's worker (`coverage-optimization-rapp-worker`) looks for instances due a scheduled pass (default 15, at least 1), across all worker replicas (call flow 24f). An instance is due when its `evaluateEverySeconds` (instance configuration, 60 to 86400; absent: manual only) has passed since its last pass; the KPI check of a change set needs a pass about an hour after it. Read once at the worker's start. Seconds, not a secret.
TRAFFIC_STEERING_SCHEDULE_TICK_SECONDS: How often the Traffic Steering rApp's worker (`traffic-steering-rapp-worker`) looks for instances due a scheduled pass (default 15, at least 1), across all worker replicas (call flow 25f). An instance is due when its `evaluateEverySeconds` (instance configuration, 60 to 86400; absent: manual only) has passed since its last pass; the KPI check of a steering step needs a pass about an hour after it. Read once at the worker's start. Seconds, not a secret.
ORAN_SIM_COUNT: Compose `oran-sim` profile: how many simulated O-DUs of the O-RAN-SC simulator to start (default 2; ADR 0012). Each gets its own address and hostname, the `sourceName` of its VES events.
ORAN_SIM_NETCONF_PASSWORD: Compose `oran-sim` profile: given to `ran-nf-oam` as `NETCONF_CRED_ORANSIM_PASSWORD`, the NETCONF password of the endpoints registered with `credentialRef: oransim`. Set it to the simulator image's built-in, public password, `netconf!`. Empty (the default): RAN NF OAM has no such credential.
ORAN_SIM_SOURCE: Compose `oran-sim` profile: the source the simulator image is built from, the named build context `pynts` of `oran-sim/Dockerfile` (default: O-RAN-SC sim-o1-ofhmp-interfaces at the pinned m-release commit). A local clone's path works too.
